rationale: UPHELD. Card file SHA256 matched 0f3fb77547b3446f985d36ba2e649e2bc1aa05228484d1d4fdf4c5ab632e0dce; original PDF SHA256 matched 3bce4d490526a69516217faf43b66b62adf565a388b622f6d1e9225faffdcdf5. I independently rendered and visually inspected PDF page 45, printed page 816, including the heading, entire paragraph, signature/date, and [No. 5595]. The sole command covers flags on the White House and public buildings in the District of Columbia and Ohio, 'at half mast to-day and on the day of the funeral service at Cincinnati, Ohio, Saturday, April 11, 1931.' The signature date is April 9, 1931. The supplied operative quotation matches the scan apart from OCR spacing. The April 11 obligation remains after April 9; an intervening day without a flag duty does not exhaust the future command. April 12, 1931 is the first civil date after the last prescribed day, so expiration_by_own_terms and the whole-order conclusion are supported. No independent continuing command, savings clause, residual authority, reporting duty, or monetary right appears between the heading and closing order number. Material limits: this source inspection does not independently reproduce the card's bounded later-source searches or prove that no historical intervening revocation ever existed. The original itself supplies the finite temporal scope, and the card identifies no contrary earlier event; no material source-text discrepancy was found.

REJECTED. Card file SHA256 matched 77bad1265048b43bcb6232726291b6d8f67cd8d00454552acc3430896e9746a0; original PDF SHA256 matched 3bce4d490526a69516217faf43b66b62adf565a388b622f6d1e9225faffdcdf5. I independently rendered and visually inspected PDF pages 622-623, printed pages 1393-1394, from the EO 5989 heading through [No. 5989]. This is one personal retirement exemption for Dr. Charles Orrin Townsend, Chief of the Sugar Division of the United States Tariff Commission. The controlling continuation at the top of page 1394 says he 'is hereby exempted from the provisions of that section until January 31, 1934.' The card's source quotation accurately preserves that date, but its first_end and whole_order_end of June 30, 1933 contradict the quoted temporal term. June 30, 1933 appears on page 1393 solely inside the title of the authorizing act, 'Making appropriations ... for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1933, and for other purposes'; the order does not say that date terminates the exemption or its authority. No earlier event or statutory sunset text is supplied; later_events is empty. Thus the claim that the fiscal-year end overrides the express January 1934 term is unsupported by its cited original, and own_terms_until_event is not established for June 30. The complete order contains no additional independent commands or express savings; historical accrued service/pay would not itself continue the exemption. Material uncertainty: these original pages alone cannot resolve whether a separate statute, later order, death, or separation ended the exemption earlier, nor do they independently verify the bounded later searches. Those limits preclude substituting an asserted exact earlier date without evidence. This rejection does not require deciding the inclusive/exclusive boundary of 'until January 31, 1934.'
